0.label: blank_divining_field
0.description: The smooth, worn, half-round working surface of the tray — the one area marked on this tray, covering the empty centre rather than any carving.
0.iconography: The field where iyẹ̀rọsùn powder is spread and the odù marks are drawn. Its emptiness is the point of the object: everything carved is pushed to the rim. Not a motif, but it records use.

panel.title: Arched Modakeke Ifá tray: face, lizards, birds and bound animals around a worn field
panel.summary: A rare half-round Ifá tray with a heavily used centre. The rim carries a face at the top flanked by two long lizards or dogs and then birds, and a straight lower band with a small central figure between rows of animals lying on their backs, legs up, and a crocodile at the right end.

register_readings.reading: Top of the arch (undetected): a face with a crest between beaded strands, flanked by two long quadrupeds facing away and, lower on the shoulders, two birds with hooked beaks.
Lower band (undetected): a small frontal figure at the centre between beaded strands, quadrupeds lying legs-up on either side, and a crocodile or lizard at the right corner.

panel.composition: A face-crowned arch over a straight base band; the arch is symmetrical about the face, the base centred on a small figure.
panel.narrative: The animals lying on their backs with legs in the air on the lower band look like trussed or slaughtered offerings; with the birds and lizards of the arch, the rim reads as the sacrifice that accompanies a consultation, laid out beneath Ẹ̀ṣù's face. The arched shape is unusual and may belong to a particular Modakeke workshop.
panel.hypotheses: Does not bear on 'chronicle'. The rhythm of beaded strands and animals is regular but not obviously counted.
cross_panel_links: Crocodile / lizard at the corner: FoA_04-5586 left rim, KBA_10300.
uncertainties: The only detection is the empty field; the whole rim reading is from the photograph.
The 'legs-up' animals may be a carving convention for animals in profile along a curve.
